title: Gregorian names
description: The Gregorian month names, March to February, then Sol: the names this calendar started with
origin: These are the Gregorian month names, which come from the Roman calendar, plus Sol, borrowed from Moses Cotsworth's International Fixed Calendar of the early 1900s. Each solar month runs about three weeks behind the Gregorian month with the same name.

leapWeek.name: Leap week
leapWeek.meaning: Added at the end of the year, about one year in six, so that the next year can start on the Monday after the equinox again.

months.name: March
months.meaning: Named after Mars, the Roman god of war. Martius was the first month of the early Roman year, which also began in spring.

months.name: April
months.meaning: No one is sure. It may come from the Latin aperire, to open, for opening buds, or from Aphrodite.

months.name: May
months.meaning: Named after Maia, a Roman goddess linked with growth and spring.

months.name: June
months.meaning: Named after Juno, queen of the Roman gods.

months.name: July
months.meaning: Renamed after Julius Caesar in 44 BC. Before that it was Quintilis, the fifth month.

months.name: August
months.meaning: Renamed after the emperor Augustus in 8 BC. Before that it was Sextilis, the sixth month.

months.name: September
months.meaning: From the Latin septem, seven. It was the seventh month when the Roman year began in March.

months.name: January
months.meaning: Named after Janus, the two-faced Roman god of doorways and beginnings.

months.name: February
months.meaning: Probably from Februa, the Roman purification rites held in this month. The origin of that word is not certain.

months.name: Sol
months.meaning: Latin for sun. Moses Cotsworth gave this name to the extra month in his International Fixed Calendar, 13 months of 28 days, proposed in the early 1900s. Eastman Kodak used it from 1928 to 1989.
